module: LuaJIT's jit.v module (Mike Pall, MIT license, 2005-2026): verbose mode of the JIT compiler. It prints one line per generated trace ([TRACE n file:line ...]) and per aborted trace, which helps to see which code is compiled or where the compiler falls back to the interpreter (NYI). Output defaults to stderr; file via argument or the LUAJIT_VERBOSEFILE environment variable.
usage:
local v = require('jit/v')
v.on('jit_verbose.txt')
-- code to observe
v.off()
notes: on and start are the same function (start serves the -jv command-line option).
A second call to on() first detaches the previous handlers (dumpoff).
The output file is overwritten at each start; '-' means stdout.

on.desc: Opens the output file and attaches the trace handler (jit.attach 'trace').

outfile.desc: Output file; default LUAJIT_VERBOSEFILE otherwise stderr; '-' = stdout.

start.desc: Alias of on, intended for the -jv command-line option.

off.desc: Detaches the trace handler and closes the file (except stdout/stderr).
